name: Ogmios

attributes.attribute: strength was verbal rather than physical
dragged people by chains from tongue to ear
sometimes carried the dead to the Otherworld

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ogmios was a god of the continental Celts. Lucian of Samosata, a Greek satirist of the second century C.E., linked Ogmios with Hercules. Yet the god's strength was in speech, not in the body. He was drawn as a bald man with dark skin, dragging people by chains that ran from his tongue to their ears. This image stood for the hold of eloquence over its hearers. For this brow the Celts named him Trenfher, the strong man. His great age hints that eloquence ripens with years. In some tellings Ogmios carried the dead to the Otherworld and was joined with Dis Pater.

okr.objective: Ogmios is a continental Celtic god whose power lies in speech.
